descriptor: Modular steel formwork maker and renter for infrastructure projects
lede: A Hyderabad company that designs, makes, rents and refurbishes modular steel formwork, the reusable moulds that hold concrete for bridge piers, walls and tanks, for contractors such as L&T and Tata Projects. It listed on NSE Emerge in May 2026, projects FY27 revenue of ₹95 Cr (+74%), and delivered ₹49 Cr in H1. The catch: a quarter of FY26 sales went to a UAE company its directors are interested in, and cash collection lags profit badly.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹53 Cr (+61%) at a 33% EBITDA margin; H1 FY27 revenue ₹48.7 Cr (+3x) and PAT ₹10 Cr. Management projects FY27 at ₹94.6 Cr revenue and ₹20 Cr PAT, and FY28 at ₹140 Cr; a new unit roughly triples capacity and the company is debt-free after its IPO.

₹13.5 Cr of FY26 sales (about a quarter) went to a related UAE company, which still owed ₹9.7 Cr at year-end; debtor days hit 204 and operating cash flow was ₹3 Cr. Shareholders approved related-party deals of up to ₹200 Cr per party and let a promoter director be paid up to ₹2 Cr a year. H1 FY27 fell ~10% short of the deck's own H1 target.
~26x trailing earnings and ~17x EV/EBITDA, against Sanghvi Movers at 16x and Action Construction Equipment at 27x.

blocks.text: Teamtech designs project-specific formwork with its own software (3-4 day proposals against ~15 days typical), fabricates modular T-formwork in Telangana, and earns from outright sales, project-length rentals and refurbishment of used panels. Steel modular panels last ~200 reuse cycles against 6-10 for timber, and ~80% of Indian construction still uses timber.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Teamtech earns high margins in a niche that should grow with infrastructure spending, and H1 FY27 shows the step-up the deck projects. But a large slice of revenue and receivables involves a company its own directors are interested in, so the numbers need checking against cash. Receivables, related-party sales and the full-year result against ₹94.6 Cr are what to watch.
